Well i like to go to a place near me called cinetopia. Thats the best "theater" experience to me because it has a bigger than imax screen. If i were to pick a specific movie id say the dark night in imax.
Anytime I have the theatre to myself, regardless of the movie. Have even been so lucky at IMAX. Well, there were a couple of people, but close enough.

Seeing The Dark Knight for a midnight release. I don't live in a big city, but the theater was absolutely packed, not a single open seat. Quite a few people were dressed for the occasion, including a really good Scarecrow costume and a young kid who turned his wheelchair into a batmobile. Lots of whooping and excitement during the opening sequence and everybody clapped at the end. It was a really cool community experience.

'Independence Day' in Anniston, Alabama. We were on a cross-country drive (LA to DC and back), and hit this small town theater just for the heck of it. OK movie, but there's a base nearby, and the crowd was really into it.
either Gravity IMAX (thought I was going to get sucked out into space!) or Death Proof (by the end the entire audience was hootin and hollerin and was best friends with each other)

Mad Max: Fury Road! It is the first movie that's ever made me excitedly bounce in my chair, laugh, and pump my fist in the air throughout the movie. I was literally on the edge of my seat from the excitement, humor, and fantastic shooting in that movie. I get excited just talking about it! I really need to go see it again. It was the most fun I've ever had a movie, hands down.

Is it possible to change all the text on a subverse to that of say the Hyrule font from zelda?
CSS allows you to choose a default font, yes.

Unless you have your own hosting to put the fonts on, this would be a bit of a pain unless the font happens to be on Google Fonts or a similar service.

The reason being that font embedding falls under some browsers "Cross-Domain" restrictions, meaning you can't load certain resources from one site onto another. However, if you have your own hosting, you can host the fonts there and set your server to explicitly allow cross-domain resource loading.

Another solution is downloading the font you want to use and heading over to Font Squirrel to utilize their webfont generator in "EXPERT" mode. You'll want to select the "Base64 Encode" CSS option which will convert the font file to a Base64 encoded string of text. You can then use the generated CSS in your subverse, but beware - the Base64 encoded string will be quite large and will take up a huge chunk of your allowed CSS character limit. I'd highly recommend minifying your code after it's completed if you go this route.
